Finished in Oxford White over Black Onyx, this Bronco currently has 37,749 miles and is powered by Ford's 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6 backed by the 10-speed automatic transmission and Advanced 4x4 system.  From the factory, this was already an exceptional build: Badlands, Sasquatch Package, Equipment Group 334A Lux, HOSS 2.0 suspension with Bilstein position-sensitive dampers, front and rear electronic lockers, electronic stabilizer-bar disconnect, molded hard top, heavy-duty modular front bumper, 12-inch SYNC 4, B&O premium audio, 360-degree cameras and much more.  Then somebody took it considerably further.  SUPERLIFT + FACTORY BILSTEIN SUSPENSION  The stance on this Bronco is absolutely awesome.  It has been upgraded with a Superlift suspension lift kit while retaining the factory Bilstein position-sensitive shocks front and rear that are part of the Badlands HOSS 2.0 suspension system.  That is an important distinction. This isn't a lesser Bronco that started with a basic suspension underneath it. The Badlands was engineered from the beginning as one of Ford's serious off-road Bronco configurations, with the Bilstein dampers providing a capable foundation before the Superlift system was added.  The additional lift provides the clearance necessary for the enormous tire package while giving the Bronco a much taller and more aggressive stance.  38x13.50R17 NITTO TRAIL GRAPPLER M/Ts  And these aren't 33s or even 35s. Combined with the Superlift suspension and wide Sasquatch bodywork, the proportions are spot-on.  This thing looks massive without looking ridiculous. It has the stance a properly built Bronco should have.  BAJA DESIGNS LP6 A-PILLAR LIGHTING  The lighting package is another area where quality components were used.  Mounted at the A-pillars are Baja Designs LP6 LED auxiliary lights.  These aren't inexpensive generic LED pods added just for appearance. The LP6 is a serious premium off-road light from one of the most respected names in the industry, providing tremendous auxiliary illumination while giving the Bronco an unmistakable look from the front.  The LP6s are complemented by custom LED headlights and custom LED taillights, giving the entire vehicle a more aggressive and updated appearance.  Between the LP6s, custom headlights, custom taillights, Superlift and enormous Nittos, this Bronco looks completely different from a stock Badlands.  VIJAY SIDE STEPS  It is also equipped with VIJAY side steps, which are especially useful on a Bronco sitting this tall.  They provide a much easier step into and out of the cabin while fitting nicely with the Bronco's black exterior accents. Against the Oxford White body, black hard top, black fender flares and other dark trim, they help tie the entire exterior together.  BADLANDS + SASQUATCH  THE RIGHT FOUNDATION  The modifications are great, but what really makes this Bronco special is what is underneath them.  This isn't a base Bronco made to resemble a Badlands.  It is a real Badlands equipped with the Sasquatch Package.  That means serious factory off-road hardware, including Advanced 4x4, electronic-locking front and rear differentials, electronic front stabilizer-bar disconnect and Ford's terrain-management system with G.O.A.T. Modes.  That is exactly the platform you want when you're going to build a Bronco on 38s.  Instead of spending money trying to make a lesser model mechanically resemble a Badlands/Sasquatch, the important equipment was already here from Ford.  2.7L ECOBOOST V6 + 10-SPEED AUTOMATIC  Another major selling feature is the 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6.  This is the engine we would want in a modified four-door Bronco, especially one carrying a tire package this substantial.  The twin-turbocharged V6 is paired with Ford's 10-speed automatic, giving you plenty of low-end torque and a broad gear spread for everything from normal highway driving to lower-speed off-road use.  Combined with the Advanced 4x4 system and locking differentials, this is a legitimately capable drivetrain rather than a vehicle that simply looks like an off-roader.  334A LUX PACKAGE  $5,440 FACTORY OPTION  Don't let the aggressive exterior fool you. Inside, this is a loaded Bronco.  It was ordered with Ford's desirable Equipment Group 334A Lux Package, which was a $5,440 factory option.  That package brings many of the features that separate a high-spec Bronco from the more basic trucks, including the huge 12-inch SYNC 4 touchscreen, B&O premium audio, connected navigation, 360-degree camera system, wireless charging pad, heated steering wheel, heated front seats, adaptive cruise control, enhanced voice recognition, universal garage-door opener, front and rear parking sensors and additional driver-assistance technology. description: Mercedes-Benz offers a very nice roadster of its own, the SL, this year celebrating its 50th anniversary. Ranging in price from $96,000 to $188,000, the top-performing SL65 AMG model comes with a supercharged V12 engine. Mercedes also has a deep-rooted technical partnership with McLaren Technologies, which races in Formula One with Mercedes-Benz engines, and from that relationship have already sprung the Mercedes-Benz McLaren SLR coupe and the higher-performance SLR 722 version of the coupe. The market has told the two companies that it's now time for the ultimate Mercedes-Benz roadster.  In front of all that, there is an elaborately constructed carbon fiber crash bar that can handle huge amounts of impact, after which its disposable cones crumble into dust as the impact progresses. At the rear, there is an all-aluminum independent suspension system that looks like it was ripped directly out of a racing car. No other car in the world is built quite like this one, and it is as beautiful underneath as it is brutish on the outside. The only major panels shared with the coupe are the scissor doors.  The 626-horsepower 5.5-liter supercharged V8 engine nestles under the long, long hood, breathing directly through the Mercedes-Benz star in the nose of the car, and exhausting through a compact, front-mounted exhaust system that exits through the bottom edges of the front fenders. This does three things. It works very well for emissions, keeping the catalytic converters hot. It helps the engine breathe better at higher rpm. It eliminates a lot of pipes and mufflers under the car, which has a flat bottom for aerodynamic purity. Oh, and four, it puts the sound of that V8 engine very close to the cockpit, where it can be appreciated.[!@@Additional Info@@!]Air filtration: active charcoal, Front air conditioning: automatic You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life.  When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident.  Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead. Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety.  Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians.
